rationale: Although the project addresses household/community drinking water shortages in an informal settlement in Bogotá (C1/C4), the exposure/intervention is purely technical and pedagogical project delivery—designing and implementing a rainwater harvesting and treatment system alongside One Health service-learning education—with no examination of legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure, or tariff mechanisms governing service access (fails C2; E03).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2: the paper reports a university/NGO service-learning rainwater harvesting, treatment design, and healthy-housing education project rather than analysing any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance mechanism.

evidence_quotes.quote: Rainwater Treatment in Informal Settlements with a One Health Approach and Community Service Learning
aims to transfer knowledge on a rain-water harvesting and treatment system to the community involver in the educational processes
This project encompassed territorial assessment, technological design and implementation, and edu-cation on healthy housing
